acceptance_cases.counterexample: A subagent implements against a rewritten or stale Revision 3.4 document.
acceptance_cases.given: The approved Revision 3.4 target, packet commit, document digest, manifest digest, and verdict.
acceptance_cases.invariant: B1B-1 derives from the independently approved Revision 3.4 source identity.
nonclaims: The manifest does not approve any later implementation head.
The approval does not authorize a runtime mount.
acceptance_cases.then: The complete approved packet matches before any implementation edit; later regression gates use immutable blobs and the new implementation manifest.
acceptance_cases.title: Approved base packet passes one-time preflight
acceptance_cases.when: The B1B-1 preflight runs in a clean isolated worktree.

acceptance_cases.counterexample: A documented gate passes only when PYTHONPATH or another hidden environment value is injected.
acceptance_cases.given: A clean checkout with the repository's recorded toolchain.
acceptance_cases.invariant: Every documented focused command is self-contained and reproducible.
nonclaims: A focused command is not a whole-repository CI claim.
Local success does not establish cross-machine reproducibility.
acceptance_cases.then: The commands pass without undocumented environment setup.
acceptance_cases.title: Documented commands require no hidden environment
acceptance_cases.when: A reviewer copies and runs each command exactly as written.

acceptance_cases.counterexample: A carrier accepts an unknown, missing, duplicated, or trailing field and produces canonical authority-shaped bytes.
acceptance_cases.given: The three approved untrusted carrier families and their exact field registries.
acceptance_cases.invariant: Carrier decoding has closed fields, full consumption, and no authority promotion.
nonclaims: Structural admission does not prove semantic authority.
Canonical bytes do not prove currentness.
acceptance_cases.then: Only exact carrier values are admitted and every malformed projection rejects.
acceptance_cases.title: Carrier schemas are closed and exact
acceptance_cases.when: Positive vectors and unknown, missing, duplicate, and trailing-field mutants are decoded.

acceptance_cases.counterexample: A Boolean is accepted as an integer, a negative value is admitted, or U256_MAX plus one wraps.
acceptance_cases.given: Every sequence and migration scalar uses the exact U256 domain.
acceptance_cases.invariant: Python and Rust accept exactly integers from zero through U256_MAX, excluding Boolean aliases.
nonclaims: This carrier test does not implement transition arithmetic.
It does not authorize sequence advancement.
acceptance_cases.then: Zero, one, U256_MAX minus one, and U256_MAX agree; Boolean, negative, and overflow vectors reject.
acceptance_cases.title: U256 boundaries and Boolean aliases are exact
acceptance_cases.when: The shared boundary vector corpus is executed in Python and Rust.

acceptance_cases.counterexample: A surrogate, malformed digest, uppercase digest, empty identifier, or over-bound identifier crosses the boundary.
acceptance_cases.given: Identifiers and digests have frozen scalar, length, Unicode, and lowercase-hex rules.
acceptance_cases.invariant: Text and digest admission is deterministic, bounded, and language-parity safe.
nonclaims: Identifier syntax does not authenticate a deployment.
Digest syntax does not establish preimage legitimacy.
acceptance_cases.then: Only bounded Unicode scalar identifiers and exact lowercase digests are admitted.
acceptance_cases.title: Identifier and digest boundaries reject ambiguous values
acceptance_cases.when: Shared Unicode, surrogate, length, case, and digest vectors run.

acceptance_cases.counterexample: Python and Rust serialize one admitted carrier to different bytes or roots.
acceptance_cases.given: One shared golden fixture covers all three carrier families and boundary rejections.
acceptance_cases.invariant: Python and Rust emit byte-identical canonical envelopes and domain-separated SHA-256 roots.
nonclaims: Parity does not create verifier authority.
SHA-256 parity does not prove collision resistance.
acceptance_cases.then: Every admitted byte string, root, and rejection class agrees exactly.
acceptance_cases.title: Python and Rust canonical parity is exact
acceptance_cases.when: Both implementations consume the same committed fixture.

acceptance_cases.counterexample: A carrier with initial sequence 1 or source snapshot 3 is treated as a verified migration authority.
acceptance_cases.given: Migration manifest carriers may encode untrusted values before later semantic verification.
acceptance_cases.invariant: No admitted carrier can construct a pin, migration candidate, successor, or current authority.
nonclaims: B1B-1 does not semantically verify migration constants.
B1B-1 does not execute V1-to-V2 migration.
acceptance_cases.then: The value remains an untrusted carrier and no authority-bearing type is reachable.
acceptance_cases.title: Carrier admission never promotes migration authority
acceptance_cases.when: A structurally valid carrier contains semantically wrong fixed migration values.

acceptance_cases.counterexample: A public bare-header advance, anchor-to-pin conversion, committed-state type, or publication helper appears in B1B-1.
acceptance_cases.evidence_level: fail-closed structural checker and mutation tests
acceptance_cases.given: The approved B1B-1 allowed and forbidden surfaces.
acceptance_cases.invariant: B1B-1 contains untrusted carriers and canonical infrastructure only.
nonclaims: Structural isolation does not prove later migration correctness.
Private naming alone is not an authority boundary.
acceptance_cases.then: The clean implementation passes and every premature-authority mutant is killed.
acceptance_cases.title: Structural checker enforces the unmounted scope
acceptance_cases.when: The allowed implementation and named scope-widening mutants are scanned.

acceptance_cases.counterexample: An implementation edit changes an authority-sensitive file without a mapped acceptance case or focused gate.
acceptance_cases.given: Every B1B-1 change is assigned one ATDD case before editing.
acceptance_cases.invariant: Each changed authority-boundary file has a named acceptance owner and evidence command.
nonclaims: Traceability does not replace code review.
A mapped test does not prove exhaustive correctness.
acceptance_cases.then: Unmapped changes block the phase gate and mapped changes carry exact evidence.
acceptance_cases.title: Every implementation change is acceptance-owned
acceptance_cases.when: The subagent prepares its final changed-file and acceptance-ID ledger.

acceptance_cases.counterexample: A runtime module imports the new carrier path, a dispatcher mounts it, or a datastore writes it.
acceptance_cases.evidence_level: reachability scan and structural negative test
acceptance_cases.given: The B1B-1 checkpoint is explicitly unmounted.
acceptance_cases.invariant: No runtime, migration, state, publication, or value-moving path consumes the carriers.
nonclaims: Absence of a mount does not prove future integration safety.
This checkpoint moves no value.
acceptance_cases.then: Only value, schema, admission, codec, fixture, checker, test, and documentation surfaces reference them.
acceptance_cases.title: B1B-1 remains unmounted
acceptance_cases.when: Reachability and forbidden-import checks run on the exact implementation head.

acceptance_cases.counterexample: Each mutation test copies the full repository and exhausts temporary storage before the semantic assertion runs.
acceptance_cases.given: The structural checker declares a bounded required-path inventory and each mutant needs only those inputs.
acceptance_cases.invariant: Mutation evidence copies or synthesizes only declared required paths and remains deterministic under a bounded temporary-space budget.
nonclaims: A bounded harness does not prove the checker is complete.
The test does not authorize deletion of unrelated temporary directories.
acceptance_cases.then: Every mutant reaches its intended assertion without copying the repository or exhausting disk.
acceptance_cases.title: Structural mutation fixtures are disk bounded
acceptance_cases.when: The clean and mutant contract tests build their isolated fixture trees.

acceptance_cases.counterexample: A review manifest omits changed files, hashes pre-commit bytes, or names an ancestor instead of the implementation head.
acceptance_cases.given: A completed B1B-1 implementation commit descended from the approved packet and an explicit changed-file inventory.
acceptance_cases.invariant: Independent review receives every implementation and evidence file at the exact committed head while approved architecture blobs remain byte-identical.
nonclaims: The implementation manifest does not approve its own contents.
An exact-head local packet is not a green CI claim.
acceptance_cases.then: The generated implementation packet is complete, source-current, sorted, and bound to one exact implementation commit.
acceptance_cases.title: Exact-head implementation packet is independently reproducible
acceptance_cases.when: The packet builder and source-manifest checker run after the implementation commit.

acceptance_cases.counterexample: A decoded anchor claim or transaction-selected value constructs the deployment verifier.
acceptance_cases.given: A later pinned verifier must originate before transaction evaluation.
acceptance_cases.invariant: Deployment pin authority remains distinct from every decoded carrier.
nonclaims: No pinned verifier is implemented in B1B-1.
Governance selection of the pin remains out of scope.
acceptance_cases.then: The B1B-2 design exposes no public claim-to-pin conversion.
acceptance_cases.title: Pinned verifier origin is independent
acceptance_cases.when: The proposed verifier interface and constructor boundary are falsified.

acceptance_cases.counterexample: A manifest and its root are changed together after verification while the independent pin is absent.
acceptance_cases.given: The manifest root and deployment ID are independently pinned.
acceptance_cases.invariant: Every migration derivation repeats manifest-root and deployment comparisons against the pin.
nonclaims: No migration derivation is implemented in B1B-1.
The pin does not establish political authority.
acceptance_cases.then: Coordinated carrier mutation cannot preserve the independent provenance relation.
acceptance_cases.title: Manifest identity remains bound to the pin
acceptance_cases.when: The B1B-2 source-bound signature and use sites are reviewed.

acceptance_cases.counterexample: Migration derives from a bundle-carried or historical V1 state while the store-current state differs.
acceptance_cases.given: A migration publication transaction can load the exact current V1 state.
acceptance_cases.invariant: Migration candidate derivation is a deterministic function of the pin, manifest, exact store-current V1 state, and validated initial configuration.
nonclaims: Datastore linearizability remains a later checkpoint.
No publication path is authorized.
acceptance_cases.then: Bundle-carried state is equality material only and stale states reject.
acceptance_cases.title: Migration uses the store-current exact V1 state
acceptance_cases.when: The B1B-2 relation is checked against currentness and stale-state witnesses.

acceptance_cases.counterexample: Migration silently changes a retained namespace, carries nonzero legacy dust, or chooses variable 0/1/0 and 4-to-5 constants.
acceptance_cases.given: The V1 and proposed V2 namespace inventories are explicit.
acceptance_cases.invariant: All retained namespaces are exact identities, V1 fee dust is zero, V2 fee apportionment is canonically empty, and fixed constants are 0/1/0 and 4-to-5.
nonclaims: The V2 committed-state schema remains a later checkpoint.
No fee allocator is mounted.
acceptance_cases.then: Every namespace and fixed constant has one named equality or rejection.
acceptance_cases.title: Migration projection is explicit and deterministic
acceptance_cases.when: The reference transition design is compared field by field.

acceptance_cases.counterexample: A durable verified-authority wrapper reaches migration after the independent pinned verifier has left the relation.
acceptance_cases.given: Hostile coordinated mutation remains in scope.
acceptance_cases.invariant: The pin is an explicit input at each migration-authority use.
nonclaims: A future implementation may choose a different non-transferable capability representation after review.
B1B-1 creates no authority wrapper.
acceptance_cases.then: Self-consistent mutation cannot replace independent provenance.
acceptance_cases.title: Migration authority does not survive without the pin
acceptance_cases.when: The design searches for transferable verified wrappers and mutation gaps.

acceptance_cases.counterexample: Commit-time migration trusts a prederived candidate or uses a pin argument that is never read.
acceptance_cases.given: Publication later receives the store-current V1 state and the pinned verifier.
acceptance_cases.invariant: Commit-time publication rederives the complete migration candidate with the pin and store-current state.
nonclaims: B1B-2 does not authorize a datastore mount.
Crash recovery remains a later checkpoint.
acceptance_cases.then: A pin-ignored or bundle-state mutant is named and must fail before later promotion.
acceptance_cases.title: Migration publication must rederive with the pin
acceptance_cases.when: The later publication contract is traced from each independent source.

acceptance_cases.counterexample: A source-binding comparison is deleted, a second migration route is added, or V2-to-V1 downgrade becomes representable.
acceptance_cases.given: Every B1B-2 authority comparison has a named negative mutant.
acceptance_cases.invariant: The later implementation cannot omit a load-bearing source relation without killing evidence.
nonclaims: Named mutants are planned evidence until implemented.
A mutation inventory is not a proof.
acceptance_cases.then: The design packet maps each authority fact to its independent source and killing test.
acceptance_cases.title: B1B-2 has a permanent falsification inventory
acceptance_cases.when: A reviewer deletes or substitutes each proposed source comparison.

acceptance_cases.counterexample: A subagent begins B1B-2 implementation without a new committed ATDD contract revision, exact B1B-1 implementation approval identity, exact B1B-2 design approval identity, or explicit user implementation authority.
acceptance_cases.given: A new committed ATDD contract revision, exact B1B-1 implementation approval identity, exact B1B-2 design approval identity, and explicit user implementation authority are four independent gates.
acceptance_cases.invariant: B1B-2 execution remains unauthorized until one new committed ATDD contract revision records the exact B1B-1 and B1B-2 approval identities and explicit user implementation authority.
nonclaims: A passing B1B-1 suite does not approve B1B-2.
Subagent consensus does not replace independent review.
acceptance_cases.then: The checker rejects B1B-2 execution unless all four source-pinned promotion conditions hold.
acceptance_cases.title: B1B-2 execution has a closed promotion gate
acceptance_cases.when: The phase matrix is checked before subagent assignment.

B1B-2.promotion_gate: new committed ATDD contract revision + exact B1B-1 implementation approval identity + exact B1B-2 design approval identity + explicit user implementation authority

probity.normative_gate: repository ATDD matrix, deterministic checker, and executable tests

design_packet.inventory_rule: all committed paths changed from the exact independently approved B1B-1 packet commit through the design target, plus immutable authority and exact B1B-1 approval sources
design_packet.packet_relation: documentation-only packet commit exactly one child of design target
